title: Graded service queues with credit-safe tier spillover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Free-tier burst patterns and uneven tenant consumption occasionally starve higher-paying routes during regional capacity constraints. Existing per-tier buckets are too coarse: they either cut a tenant off abruptly or allow a burst to consume a global credit pool, causing latency SLO violations for paid/enterprise customers.

Goal: Implement graded service queues that provide progressive spillover between free, paid, and enterprise tiers while preserving quota guarantees for higher tiers. The solution should be quota-aware, region-aware, and allow controlled progressive demotion (soft-degradation) rather than hard failures.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement billing changes, long-term quota reconciliation jobs, or per-model fine-grained pricing. It focuses on routing/admission behaviour and observability.

Success metrics: reduction in paid-tier 95th percentile tail latency under multi-tenant bursts (target: -25%), reduction in paid-tier request failures during cross-region capacity events (target: >90% successful fallbacks), clear dashboards showing credit consumption and spillover events.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces per-region per-tier soft caps and prevents free-tier bursts from reducing paid-tier effective throughput below configured reserve
Fallback chain supports fallback to smaller-quantized model variants for free/paid tiers when regional capacity is limited
Dashboard shows live credit reservoirs per-region and per-tier and records spillover events with tenant ids anonymized
Integration tests covering at least three scenarios: normal load, free-tier burst, and region outage with cross-region spillover
Canary rollout plan and rollback playbook documented and verified in staging
implementation_notes: Introduce a per-region credit reservoir: credits_consumed/credits_reserved semantics with sliding window decay to allow short spikes
Graded queues: implement three queue classes (free/paid/enterprise) with admission priorities and a progressive spillover policy that preserves enterprise reservations first

Admission controller logic in router: check(tenant_tier, region) => allocate_from(reservoirs). If primary reservoir depleted, attempt fast path to fallback reservoir with throttle multiplier; if fallback hits reserve threshold, demote to model-variant fallback instead of dropping request
Config knobs: tier_reserve_pct, spillover_step_ms, token_decay_window_sec, min_reserve_absolute
Observability: emit events: credit_alloc, credit_spill, fallback_triggered, fallback_resolved, reserve_violation. Map to console-graphs and alerts
Testing: synthetic workload generator that can simulate 10k tenants with configurable burstiness, and unit-tests for admit/release correctness
tasks: Design schema for per-region reservoirs and tier reserves
Implement router admission controller with spillover policy
Add metrics and tracing for credit events
Implement model-variant fallback path and compatibility validation
E2E tests and chaos scenario in staging (region failover)
Canary rollout to 10% of traffic + monitor + rollback plan
